title: Pour Water
summary: Given an elevation map represented as an integer array heights, where heights[i] denotes the height of the terrain at index i, and an integer volume, water will initially fall at index k.
statement: Given an elevation map represented as an integer array heights, where heights[i] denotes the height of the terrain at index i, and an integer volume, water will initially fall at index k. The water will rest on the highest terrain or water level at that index. It will then flow left if it would eventually fall left, flow right if it would eventually fall right, or remain in place if neither direction is lower. Assume the terrain extends infinitely high at the boundaries, and water must occupy exactly one grid block.
constraints: Each unit falls at k, preferring the left side if following a nonincreasing path reaches a lower level.
If left cannot fall, try right by the same rule; otherwise remain at k.
Return final column levels after all units settle.
hints: Simulate one unit at a time.
Scan left across nonincreasing levels while remembering the latest strict drop; only if none exists scan right.
Increase the chosen column by one.
The scan order implements left preference and the last lower point is where gravity ultimately settles the unit.
editorial: The scan order implements left preference and the last lower point is where gravity ultimately settles the unit.

tests.explanation: Two units settle left, one right, and one at k.
Both units travel left to the lowest reachable positions.
